sample_unit: individuals (226 with type 1 diabetes in REPLACE-BG; 207 in external cohort)

links.outcome: Glucose prediction performance on external validation cohort versus development dataset
links.effect: GluLLM had lower 30-min RMSE than the strongest baseline on REPLACE-BG and on the external Móstoles cohort (20.6 ± 3.5 and 9.6 ± 2.9 mg/dL; p < 0.001); hypoglycaemia AUROC 0.79 and 0.84.
links.quote: We trained and evaluated GluLLM on the REPLACE-BG dataset, which includes 226 individuals with type 1 diabetes, and validated it on an external cohort comprising 207 individuals with type 2 diabetes or without diabetes.

unlisted_practices: On-device deployment of lightweight LLMs to preserve privacy and avoid transmitting sensitive data to remote servers
Domain-specific adaptation of pretrained LLMs through multimodal adaptor modules for glucose forecasting
Smartphone computational feasibility testing (CPU, memory, latency)

screen.reason: The study develops and validates a multimodal LLM adaptor framework (GluLLM) for on-device glucose forecasting, assessing accuracy and smartphone device feasibility (latency/resource use) without testing a clinical deployment practice or safeguard.
